entries.definition: A previously working behavior that stops working after a change.
entries.plain: You fixed or changed something and broke an old capability.
entries.example: A new tool router causes an existing evaluation to fail.

entries.definition: A test added or retained to ensure a previously fixed failure does not return.
entries.plain: A test that prevents the same bug coming back.
entries.example: Reproduce a bug in a test before fixing it.

entries.definition: A detailed record of what happened during an agent run.
entries.plain: The execution history you inspect when debugging the agent.
entries.example: Prompts, tool calls, outputs, errors and timing.

entries.definition: The sequence of decisions, actions and states an agent followed to reach an outcome.
entries.plain: The path the agent took.
entries.example: Two agents can reach the same answer through very different trajectories.

entries.definition: One complete attempt by a model or agent to perform a task.
entries.plain: One run from start to finish.
entries.example: Run ten rollouts of the same task to estimate reliability.

entries.definition: The probability that at least one correct result appears among k attempts.
entries.plain: How likely you are to get one success if you try several times.
entries.example: Pass@5 can be high even if pass@1 is modest.

entries.definition: Using a model to evaluate another model or agent output.
entries.plain: An AI grades another AI.
entries.example: A judge scores whether a response follows a rubric.

entries.definition: Model-generated information that appears plausible but is unsupported or false.
entries.plain: The model makes something up.
entries.example: Citing a function that does not exist in the repository.

entries.definition: A model optimized to spend more computation working through difficult problems before answering or acting.
entries.plain: A model designed to think harder on complex tasks.
entries.example: Use more reasoning effort for architecture or debugging than for simple rewriting.

entries.definition: The process used to select model outputs from possible next tokens or actions.
entries.plain: How the model chooses among possible continuations.
entries.example: Different sampling settings can produce different valid answers.

entries.definition: A parameter traditionally used to control randomness in model sampling.
entries.plain: Higher values usually mean more variation.
entries.example: Not all modern reasoning APIs expose or emphasize temperature.

entries.definition: The time required for an operation or response to complete.
entries.plain: How long you wait.
entries.example: Tool calls and long reasoning can increase agent latency.

entries.definition: The amount of work a system can process in a given period.
entries.plain: How much work gets done per unit time.
entries.example: Requests per second or tasks per hour.

entries.definition: Stored previous work that can be reused instead of recomputed or fetched again.
entries.plain: Remember a result so you do not pay to redo it.
entries.example: Reuse processed context across repeated model calls.

entries.definition: Reuse of previously processed prompt or context content across model calls.
entries.plain: Avoid reprocessing identical context.
entries.example: A large stable system prompt can be cached.

entries.definition: A requested item is already present in a cache and can be reused.
entries.plain: The cache had what you needed.
entries.example: No need to recompute an embedding.

entries.definition: A requested item is not present in a cache and must be computed or fetched.
entries.plain: The cache did not have it.
entries.example: A new document must be embedded before search.

entries.definition: The maximum amount of model tokens allocated to a task, response or process.
entries.plain: How much model text/computation you are willing to spend.
entries.example: Limit an agent to a fixed context and output budget.

entries.definition: The amount of computational effort allocated to a model or agent task.
entries.plain: How much processing you let the system spend.
entries.example: Use a larger reasoning budget only for difficult tasks.

entries.definition: Application Programming Interface; a defined way for software components to communicate.
entries.plain: A contract between pieces of software.
entries.example: get_frame(frame_id) returns a frame.

entries.definition: Model Context Protocol; a protocol for exposing tools and contextual resources to AI applications in a standardized way.
entries.plain: A standard connection between AI applications and external capabilities.
entries.example: Expose repository tools to multiple compatible AI clients.

entries.definition: An API designed so agents can discover, understand and use it reliably.
entries.plain: An API whose semantics and errors make sense to machines as well as humans.
entries.example: Stable names, structured outputs, explicit errors and bounded operations.

entries.definition: A machine-readable description of data, fields or tool arguments.
entries.plain: The shape and rules of structured data.
entries.example: frame_id is an integer and must be positive.
